Hero.headline: Natural Code,
Hero.description: Hüma is a high-performance programming language featuring native Turkish syntax. Built with a Rust-backed core, it combines the expressiveness of natural language with the raw speed of a systems compiler.

IDE_Page.headline: Code with Precision,
IDE_Page.description: Hüma IDE is a high-performance, lightweight development environment designed specifically for the Hüma language. It features a custom terminal, Monaco editor integration, and native performance through Tauri.

monaco.title: Monaco Editor
monaco.desc: The same high-performance editor that powers VS Code. Syntax highlighting, auto-completion, and native suffix support.

terminal.title: Integrated Terminal
terminal.desc: Run and compile your Hüma programs without leaving the editor. Instant feedback on standard output and error.

tauri.title: Zero-Latency Core
tauri.desc: Built with Tauri and Rust for a lightweight footprint and maximum speed. No Electron bloat, just performance.

natural_syntax.title: Natural Syntax
natural_syntax.description: Code using Turkish suffixes that feel natural and improve readability.

hybrid_execution.title: Hybrid Execution
hybrid_execution.description: Mix interpretation for development speed and compilation for production power.

standalone_compilation.title: Standalone Binary
standalone_compilation.description: Compile your code to a single, statically linked binary for any system.

standard_library.title: Standard Library
standard_library.description: Built-in modules for math, file handling, statistics and more.

CTA.headline: Start Building Now
CTA.description: Join the community of developers building the next generation of software with Hüma.
CTA.available_platforms: Available on Windows, macOS, and Linux

introduction.title: Intro & Philosophy
introduction.description: Discover Hüma's design principles and why it's so fast.
introduction.hero_title: New Wings of Modern Software: Hüma
introduction.hero_desc: Hüma is not just a programming language; it's an ecosystem designed to maximize Developer Experience (DX). It combines the safety of Rust with the natural suffix system of Turkish.

cognitive_ease.title: Cognitive Ease
cognitive_ease.desc: Coding in a natural language structure removes barriers between logical thought and syntax, reducing the margin for error.

agglutination.title: Suffix System
agglutination.desc: Hüma's unique suffix system increases readability while converting into pure performance at compile time.

industrial.title: Industrial Strength
industrial.desc: Unlike loose-typed languages, Hüma provides a robust infrastructure that can be used safely in critical systems.

why_huma.title: Why Hüma?
points: Safety Built on Top of Rust

syntax.title: Basic Syntax
syntax.description: Variables, data types, and Hüma's unique suffix system.
syntax.hero_desc: Hüma's syntax offers logical clarity and flexibility. In this section, we'll examine variable definition, data types, and the heart of the language: the 'Suffix System'.

variables.title: Variable Definition
variables.desc: In Hüma, everything is a value. You can define both local and global variables with the 'olsun' keyword.

suffix_system.title: Suffix System
suffix_system.desc: Hüma supports Turkish's agglutinative structure at the compiler level. All suffixes following the apostrophe (') are automatically stripped by the compiler, achieving both natural language and high performance.

conditionals.title: Conditionals (ise / yoksa)
conditionals.desc: Control the flow of your application with natural language logic. Hüma uses 'ise' (if) and 'yoksa' (else) keywords.

loops.title: Loops (olduğu sürece / range)
loops.desc: Use 'olduğu sürece' for conditional loops, and 'dan ... e kadar' for numerical ranges.

postfix_calls.title: Particle and Postfix Calls
postfix_calls.desc: Hüma supports 'ile' (with) and 'yükle' (load) structures compatible with Turkish syntax.

grammar.title: Grammar & Suffix System
grammar.description: Understanding Hüma's Turkish natural language structure and its runtime interaction.
grammar.hero_desc: Hüma optimizes the agglutinative structure of Turkish at the compiler level. Grammatical suffixes added via an apostrophe (') improve readability without introducing any performance overhead.

mechanics.title: How it Works?
mechanics.desc: Traditional languages use separate keywords for every operation. Hüma allows you to add suffixes directly to variable names. These suffixes are extracted by the Lexer during compilation, ensuring your code remains as fast as pure Rust while reading like a book.

suffixes.title: Standard Suffixes
suffixes.desc: Hüma supports the most common Turkish noun state suffixes. Using these instead of stand-alone keywords is the recommended 'idiomatic' way to write Hüma.

accusative.name: Accusative (-i, -ı)
accusative.usage: Used for printing or sending objects to functions.

dative.name: Dative (-e, -a)
dative.usage: Used for adding items to collections or navigating.

ablative.name: Ablative (-den, -dan)
ablative.usage: Used for removing items or defining ranges.

genitive.name: Genitive (-nin, -ın)
genitive.usage: Used for accessing object properties or methods. The trailing possessive suffix (hızı'ı) is now optional.

possessive.name: Possessive Suffixes
possessive.usage: Used to express object properties more naturally.

plural.name: Plural Suffixes
plural.usage: Used when operating on lists or multiple objects.

equality.name: Equality Case (-ce)
equality.usage: Used to add meaning of perspective or style.

best_practices.title: Best Practices
best_practices.desc: Suffixes are purely cosmetic at the VM level but essential for human readability. Using suffixes like 'ın or 'in for object access is preferred over dot notation.

cli.title: CLI Reference
cli.description: Complete guide for all Hüma command-line interface tools.
cli.hero_desc: Hüma follows a bilingual CLI design. You can use English or Turkish commands interchangeably.

execution.title: Execution & REPL
execution.run: huma run <target> — Run a source file or a package script.
execution.repl: huma repl — Start the interactive shell.
execution.ide: huma ide — Launch the desktop developer environment.

compilation.title: Compilation & VM
compilation.build: huma build <file> — Compile source to .hbc bytecode.
compilation.exec: huma exec <file> — Run compiled bytecode on the VM.
compilation.gen: huma gen <file> — Generate standalone Rust source code.

package.title: Package Management
package.init: huma init — Initialize a new project.
package.new: huma new <name> — Create a project in a new folder.
package.install: huma install — Install dependencies from huma.json.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.update: huma update — Self-update the Hüma binary.
maintenance.version: huma version — Display current version info.

functions_classes.title: Functions & Classes
functions_classes.description: Modern object-oriented programming and functional structures.
functions_classes.hero_desc: Hüma supports both functional and object-oriented programming paradigms. In this section, you'll learn how to make your code modular and how to build complex data structures.

functions.title: Functions
functions.desc: Functions are the fundamental building blocks of Hüma. You can easily manage data flow with 'alsın' and 'döndür' structures.

classes.title: Classes (Object-Oriented)
classes.desc: Classes in Hüma are powerful structures that hold data and behavior together. You can access object properties with the 'bu' (self) keyword.

methods.title: Methods & 'bu' Call
methods.desc: Inside a method belonging to an object, the object itself is accessed with the 'bu' keyword. This is the cornerstone of object-oriented programming.

lists_errors.title: Data Structures & Errors
lists_errors.description: Advanced data structures (Dictionaries, Lists) and safe error handling techniques.
lists_errors.hero_desc: Hüma offers advanced tools for managing your application's data flow and handling unexpected situations. Handle data sets with Lists and Dictionaries, and prevent crashes with the 'dene...yakala' structure.

lists.title: Lists & Dictionaries
lists.desc: Hüma lists are dynamic. Dictionaries (Maps) are optimized for storing key-value pairs.

errors.title: Structural Error Handling
errors.desc: Provides a safe exit strategy for bottlenecks in your programs. Use'dene...yakala' (try...catch) to catch errors and assign the message to a variable.

stdlib.title: Standard Library
stdlib.description: Hüma's built-in API reference and helper modules.
stdlib.hero_desc: Hüma comes with a rich set of built-in libraries to speed up your development process. Everything from mathematics to the file system is optimized.
stdlib.import_info: Use the 'yükle' directive to include a module in your project:

modules.renkler: ANSI color outputs for current terminals.
modules.dosya: File read, write, and line splitting.
modules.istatistik: Mean, variance, and standard deviation calculations.
modules.rastgele: Random number generation and list shuffling.
modules.birim_test: Unit test framework: test_et, iddia_et, test_raporu.

compiler.title: Compiler Internals
compiler.description: Deep-dive into the Hüma compiler pipeline: lexer, suffix system, AST, and interpreter.
compiler.hero_desc: Hüma is a high-performance interpreter powered by Rust. Your source code is first tokenized, then transformed into a syntax tree, and finally executed by traversing the tree.

pipeline.title: The Pipeline
pipeline.desc: Hüma source code passes through four main stages: Source Text, Lexer (Tokenizer), Parser, and Interpreter.

lexer.title: Lexer & Suffix System
lexer.desc: The Hüma lexer strips Turkish grammatical suffixes (i'yi, yı, nı etc.) at compile time to determine the root word. This process has zero runtime cost.

ast.title: Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)
ast.desc: The parser transforms the token stream into a tree of Rust enums. Each node represents a language construct: statements, expressions, and blocks.

build.title: Build from Source
build.desc: To build the Hüma compiler on your machine, a stable Rust toolchain (rustup) is required.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.description: Official update history of the Hüma language and toolchain.
changelog.hero_desc: Hüma is constantly evolving. In every version, you can track new language features, performance improvements, and community-driven bug fixes here.

changes: Postfix Load: "file.hb"'yi yükle syntax for more natural module loading.
Particle Call: '10 ile 20'yi topla' style function calls matching Turkish sentence structure.
Extended Suffixes: Possessive ('si), Plural ('lar), Equality ('ce), and Accusative ('ni) suffixes added to Lexer.
Range Loop: x = 0'dan 10'a kadar { ... } syntax added.
Object Method Context: 'kendisi' context is now automatic when calling methods on plain objects.
Optional Possessive: Removed mandatory trailing 'si/ı' suffix for 'nin' access.
Postfix Load: "file.hb"'yi yükle syntax for more natural module loading.
Particle Call: '10 ile 20'yi topla' style function calls matching Turkish sentence structure.
Extended Suffixes: Possessive ('si), Plural ('lar), Equality ('ce), and Accusative ('ni) suffixes added to Lexer.
Range Loop: x = 0'dan 10'a kadar { ... } syntax added.
Object Method Context: 'kendisi' context is now automatic when calling methods on plain objects.
Optional Possessive: Removed mandatory trailing 'si/ı' suffix for 'nin' access.
Structural Error Handling: Support for catching and managing errors with 'dene...yakala' blocks.
Native Dictionary (Sözlük) Type: High-performance key-value maps with {} syntax.
Dictionary Methods: Programmatic access with .getir() and .ayarla() methods.
Dictionary Suffix System: Natural language access like 'sozluk'ten key'i getir'.
VM Opcode Expansion: Added TryBlockStart, TryBlockEnd, and MakeMap to bytecode level.
Enhanced JSON Hardening: Standardized JSON serialization support for Dictionaries.
Package Manager Security Hardening: closed path traversal, RCE/code injection, and command injection vulnerabilities.
SHA-256 Integrity Verification: package hash checks added to huma.lock.
Atomic File Writes: metadata and lock files now use write-then-rename for safety.
Recursive Dependency Installation: deep dependency trees with cycle detection.
Native Code Safety Warning: --güvenilir (--trusted) flag for packages with embedded Rust code.
Library Standardization: version/author/dependency headers added to all lib/*.hb files.
Function Shadowing Cleanup: resolved Rust built-in conflicts in dizgi.hb and dosya.hb.
GUI Module Migration: gui.hb is no longer built-in, now loadable from huma_modulleri/gui/.
PaketMetadata Extension: github and lisans (license) fields added.
Typo Fixes: YESIL→YEŞİL, iceriyor_mu→içeriyor_mu.
Native Package Architecture: support for direct integration of Rust Crates (Cargo) into Hüma projects.
Official SQLite Support: high-performance local database module based on rusqlite (huma_sqlite).
Full Standalone Compilation: 'huma gen' now produces full Cargo projects containing all native dependencies.
Database Object Mapping: automatic conversion of SQL query results to Hüma objects.
Hüma CLI Improvements: automatic Cargo guidance after standalone project generation.
Modern Networking: added high-performance HTTP client via ag_istekleri library.
Huma Server (HTTP): built-in web server framework with dynamic route management.
Bilingual CLI: all commands are now usable in both Turkish and English.
Byte Data Type: built-in support for processing images, audio and other binary files.
Package Manager 2.0: script support, integrity checks and automated git integration.
Server Response Headers: object-based header support for customizing HTTP responses.
Native Graphical User Interface (GUI) library (gui.hb) launched based on egui.
Launched the 'Hüma Kütüphaneleri' community sharing platform.
Added high-performance web server support with the new 'huma_sunucu' core module.
Advanced Package Manager (huma paket) and GitHub integration added.
huma.lock lockfile system implemented for reproducible builds.
SemVer compatible version control and package metadata (huma.json) introduced.
Full Bilingual CLI support (e.g., 'run' or 'çalıştır', 'build' or 'derle').
npm-style package scripts support with 'baslat'/'start' preference.
Optimized syntax and drawing loops for GUI modules.
Workspace Architecture: Project split into modular crates: huma-core, huma-compiler, and huma-cli.
VS Code Extension: Official syntax highlighting and language support extension for VS Code.
Modern Web Interface: Documentation site and IDE rebuilt with Vite and React.
Internationalization (i18n): Multi-language support for documentation and the website.
Unified CLI: consolidation of all tools under a single binary with --ide support.
Tauri IDE: Portable desktop IDE with built-in file access and saving capabilities.
NLP Library: Text processing, analysis, and natural language tools (nlp.hb).
Syntax Improvements: More flexible structures for variable assignment, control flow, and function definitions.
New Rust-Based Architecture: Complete rewrite to Rust.
Bytecode Virtual Machine (VM): High-performance execution engine.
Standalone Binary Compilation: Ability to compile scripts into native executables.
REPL: Interactive shell environment.
Module System: Library support via 'yükle' (load) command.

getting_started.title: Getting Started
getting_started.description: Install Hüma on your system and write your first high-performance program in minutes.
getting_started.hero_desc: Welcome to the Hüma ecosystem — a high-performance language designed for precision and kinetic speed. This guide will help you optimize your environment and write your first professional Hüma program.

installation.title: Installation
installation.desc: The Hüma toolchain natively supports Windows, Linux, and macOS (x64/ARM64) architectures. Our installation script automatically detects your system's hardware.
installation.arch_desc: Hüma runs with zero latency on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3) and modern x86_64 processors. The compiler core is built using safe, high-performance Rust.

quick_start.title: Verification & REPL
quick_start.desc: Verify your installation and start experimenting immediately in the interactive shell (REPL).

first_project.title: Your First Project
first_project.desc: Hüma's package manager creates a professional project structure with just one command. This sets up your manifest, boilerplate, and dependency management.
first_project.suffix_desc: The 'huma paket yeni' command automatically generates a 'huma.json' file and a main entry point, preparing your project for scale from day one.
